newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's mazut trade sees '96 exports flat or down.
newsitem.headline: Russia's mazut trade sees '96 exports flat or down.

text.p: Russian fuel oil traders said on Thursday that exports this year were flat or lagging on 1995 levels, and that Russia's biggest oil producer, LUKoil, was making moves to crowd other operators out of the export market.
"Volumes this year have been flat -- we were expecting them to be one and a half times higher," said one trader, adding that his company's revenues slipped ten percent last month.
"It's a very strange market right now," a second trader said. "There should be a lot more exports, but it's choppy."
Traders said LUKoil chartered its own vessel out of St Petersburg on Thursday for the first time, sending out 28,000 tonnes of mostly M-40 grade material.
"LUKoil has come onto the market," said one trader, adding that previously, the company traded fuel oil, known locally as mazut, only through other firms.
LUKoil officials declined to comment.

While traders said the LUKOil shipment was part of the company's plan to export 600,000 tonnes before waterways freeze in November, they said these deliveries would not boost the total volume of mazut exported from Russia this year.

One estimated total Russian exports over mid-May to November -- when exports traditionally soar as the winter heating season ends and refineries seek to unload stocks -- would be down ten to 15 to possibly 20 percent on last year.
Traders said limited capacity at St Petersburg meant LUKoil could send out its vessels only by crowding other players out.
"It's impossible to exist side-by-side in this market -- you have to push others out," said one, adding that one big player formerly active on the Petersburg market was gone this year.

"Barges haven't been loading as much," a second trader said, referring to continuing low water levels on the Volga River, a key waterway which regional refineries use to ship material up to St Petersburg and out to northwest Europe or over to Ukrainian and Russian outlets and out to the Mediterranean.

The state customs committee, in figures carried by Interfax news agency, said total mazut exports over January-July were nearly 11.22 million tonnes, a decline of 1.87 million tonnes, or 14.1 percent, on year-ago levels.

July export levels dipped 6.5 percent year-on-year to 2.08 million tonnes, it said. European traders and analysts estimated this week that of this, 1.7 to 1.9 million tonnes were exported to western Europe.

State statistics committee figures put Russia's total mazut production over January-July at 37.8 million tonnes, a slip of three percent on year-ago volumes, with July output alone at 4.8 million tonnes. No other comparative figures were given.
Russian refineries had sketchy crude supplies in August as the government sought to secure oil for its federal programme, but one trader said refinery runs would pick up this month.
Russia's federal programme includes oil deliveries, often as barter, to former Soviet-era clients such as Eastern Europe and Cuba.
"I know one client that was supposed to get 30-50,000 tonnes of mazut in August from Ufa and instead got 3,000 tonnes of gasoil -- that's it," one trader said.
Industry sources said there was a growing desire by producers like LUkoil to export for themselves.
"Middlemen have no place," one said.
-- Lynnley Browning, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
